entry.name: Daimon-Infinity DM-DataDex
entry.title: TacExoGaze: A Human-Centric Glove Interface for Multi-View Vision-Tactile Data Collection in Dexterous Manipulation
entry.venue: Dataset release (Hugging Face, ModelScope), 2026-04-15; TacExoGaze preprint forthcoming
entry.summary: Both hands of human operators in the TacExoGaze exoskeleton (DM-DataDex) with vision-based DM-Tac X sensors on the thumb, index and middle fingertips, released as per-sensor deformation, shear and depth maps alongside exoskeleton finger encoders, wrist, head and eye tracking, stereo headset video and an RGB-D third view over 22 tabletop tasks.
entry.hand: Human hands wearing the TacExoGaze exoskeleton glove (DM-DataDex), both hands

sensor.note: Three fingertip sensors per hand (thumb, index, middle; 6 per session when both hands are recorded). Per sensor and frame: a deformation map and a shear map (3 planes each) and a depth map (1 plane), uint16, lossless FFV1 in .mov. 802 sessions (2026-01-23 to 03-03): 320x240 maps at 20 fps. 393 sessions tagged newtac/tacV2 (2026-03-19 to 04-03): 384x288 maps at 30 fps plus the raw 640x480 grayscale sensor image (H.264 mp4). Deformation/shear values sit around 30,000 (offset encoding); scale and units are not documented in the card (decoding is left to the Daimon SDK in the gated Daimon-Infinity-Lite repo).
sensor.model: DM-Tac X (label in the card's DM-DataDex figure: 'DM-Tac X 120FPS Vision-based Tactile Sensors')

scale.text: DM-DataDex part: ~45.1 h, 10,015 episodes in 1,195 sessions, 22 tabletop tasks, 3.93M frames at 20 or 30 fps; ~4% of the hours and 6% of the 37.75 TB in the Daimon-Infinity release (card pie chart: 5%), the rest being DM-DataClaw gripper data

entry.access: Hugging Face daimonrobotics/Daimon-Infinity, folder DataDex_Datasets/ (ungated; 2.28 TB, one LeRobot v3.0 folder per session, single files downloadable); the ModelScope copy requires an application form.
caveats: This entry covers only the DM-DataDex (TacExoGaze exoskeleton) sessions in DataDex_Datasets/. The rest of Daimon-Infinity (DM-DataClaw/ and the folder named TacExo/, robot_type ugripper_left / ugripper_right / dual_ugripper, ~1,091 h and 35.5 TB) is handheld parallel-gripper (DM-DataClaw) data and is excluded; the TacExo/ folder holds gripper data despite its name.

Two recording formats: 802 sessions at 20 fps with 320x240 tactile maps and no raw sensor image; 393 sessions (folder tags newtac, tacV2) at 30 fps with 384x288 maps plus the raw 640x480 sensor image. The card describes only 384x288 maps and says video and state are unified at 30 fps.
Tactile maps are 16-bit FFV1 .mov files (not H.264), 135-250 MB per sensor per session; deformation/shear values are offset-encoded around 30,000 with no documented scale or unit.
Each stream is one concatenated file per session (5-10 episodes); episodes are cut by from/to timestamps in meta/episodes. Sessions are 0.8-7.4 GB (median 1.6 GB).

Not every session has both hands: 110 sessions record tactile on the left hand only (Orient and place blocks on peg, pen to cup, Wiping whiteboard on laptop), 15 on the right hand only, and 7 have 1-2 sensors on one hand. 43 Store Allen keys sessions have no camera streams.

One wrist pose is nearly constant (position range < 2 cm over the session) in 165 (left) and 335 (right) of 1,094 sessions checked. In the pouring sessions the third-view video shows both hands on the cup while the left wrist pose stays within ~2 mm, so wrist tracking is missing in at least some sessions.
Eye pose (gaze) is constant in 184 of 1,094 sessions, 158 of them 30 fps sessions, i.e. gaze is mostly not recorded in the newer format.

observation.state and action share the gripper/robot layout of the card (114-D / 111-D); robot, gripper and IMU dimensions are the placeholder 9930 throughout DataDex, and action equals the recorded state (human demonstration).

Upload incomplete when listed (repo last modified 2026-10-17): 28 sessions (275 episodes, 1.3 h) lack 510 of their declared video files, 8 sessions have none, and 30 lack meta/episodes and meta/stats.json.
No operator, scene or object labels: DataDex sessions have no episodes_metadata.json; the task label (meta/tasks.parquet) is the only annotation. 'Wiping the whiteboard clean' is spelled two ways.
The TacExoGaze preprint named in the card's citation is not published; the arXiv paper linked from the card (2610.20320, TacClaw-Infinity) covers the gripper data only.

unconfirmed: hours=45.1 derived: sum over the 1,195 DataDex sessions of meta/info.json total_frames / fps (802 sessions at 20 fps = 26.1 h, 393 at 30 fps = 18.9 h). Includes 1.3 h in 28 sessions whose video files are partly missing. episodes=10,015 and frames=3,927,883 are sums of total_episodes / total_frames (frames mix 20 and 30 fps).

Share of the release: DataDex_Datasets/ is 2,281,886,948,206 B of 37,748,239,156,224 B in the three data folders (HF treesize; DM-DataClaw/ 35.09 TB, TacExo/ 0.37 TB) = 6.0% by bytes. By hours, DataDex 45.1 h vs 1,090.7 h of gripper data (563 DM-DataClaw + 7 TacExo session info.json files) = 4.0%. The card's pie chart gives DM-DataDex 5%.

Hours claims conflict: the card says the first 1,000 h are released and 10,000+ h will be open-sourced, and its statistics section is 'based on approximately 1,209 hours'; QbitAI (2026-04-20) writes '其中 10000 小时数据直接开源' [of which 10,000 hours are directly open-sourced]; the TacClaw-Infinity paper and GitHub README give 10,000+ h collected; the files sum to ~1,136 h (all devices).

tasks=22: 23 task strings in meta/tasks.parquet over all sessions, two of which ('Wiping_the_whiteboard_clean', 'Wiping the whiteboard clean') are the same task. Session folder names carry extra tags (pc, laptop, newtac, tacV2, right_hand) whose meaning is not documented.

Sensor model: the card's DM-DataDex figure labels the fingertip sensors 'DM-Tac X 120FPS'. The 20 fps sessions store 320x240 maps, which matches the 320x240 sensing resolution Daimon lists for DM-Tac F, while DM-Tac X is listed at 384x288 (the size in the 30 fps sessions); which sensor the 20 fps sessions used is not stated.

Deformation and shear: 3 planes each (gbrp16le), decoded values centred on 30,000 (e.g. 29,950-30,103 in sampled frames), plane 1 never below 30,000; the TacClaw-Infinity paper calls the DM-Tac X output 'three-axis tactile signals'. Axis order, scale and unit are not documented. Tactile depth: one plane, 0 in a non-contact frame and 0-199 in a v2 frame; unit not stated.
Raw tactile images (30 fps sessions) are declared as (480, 640, 1) but stored as H.264 yuv420p 640x480; a decoded frame shows a grayscale speckle-pattern gel image.
Third-view depth: FFV1 gray16le 640x480 with intrinsics for 1280x720 / 640x480 / 640x360 in info.json; camera model and depth unit not stated.

scene_types=['lab']: from 9 third-view frames (8 tasks, 2026-01-23 to 04-01) all showing the same white table in an office-like room; the card says data were collected 'in real environments' and gives no scene list. Several different operators are visible; their number is not stated.

Wrist-tracker and gaze dropout counts come from the per-session min/max in meta/stats.json (1,094 of 1,165 files had a 114-D state; 71 had a different layout and were skipped); threshold 2 cm for wrist position, 0.02 for eye quaternion components.
action vs observation.state in tacexo_Fold_the_towels_pc_0206_110646: same values at lag 0 (mean absolute difference 1e-5, max 0.03 on eye quaternions).
fps of the egocentric and third-view streams in the 30 fps sessions taken from info.json (fps 30); ffprobe was run on 20 fps session files only (H.264 640x480 at 20 fps).

sample.fetch_estimate: ~2.8 GB if each episode is cut out of its session's stream files with ffmpeg seeks over HTTP (episode length / session length x session size: 0.39 + 0.49 + 0.21 + 0.60 + 0.33 + 0.21 + 0.41 + 0.20 GB); ~20.8 GB if the 8 whole sessions were downloaded, which exceeds the 20 GB budget, so windowed fetching is required. Re-hosted media: headset and third-view H.264 640x480 clips of 15-32 s are a few MB each; the 16-bit FFV1 tactile maps cannot be re-hosted as video and must be reduced (e.g. a coarse vector grid per sensor) to fit 2 MB of episode JSON: 6 sensors x 3 maps x 320x240 at 20 fps is far above that.
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 22 > 6, so 8 were chosen to span action types (fold, pour, write with a tool, plug/insert, place in slots, cable transfer, stack), objects (towel, cup, marker, test tubes and stoppers, Allen keys, Ethernet cable, polo shirt, cubes), one-handed (right-hand writing) and two-handed tasks, and both recording formats (5 at 20 fps / 320x240, 3 at 30 fps / 384x288 with raw sensor images). The release shows one tabletop room, so scenes cannot vary. One episode per task, all 15-33 s (inside 10-60 s, no window). Candidates came from sessions with every declared stream file present; where available, sessions in which both wrist poses and gaze vary (meta/stats.json ranges) were preferred. Contact (readings above rest for >= 1 s on the tactile maps) has not been checked: it needs the FFV1 files and must be verified at conversion, replacing an episode from the same session if it fails.
